name: ORGAN
summary: An Australian high-frequency axion-search program based primarily at the University of Western Australia, with a low-frequency branch in Melbourne.
detection_principle: A cryogenic resonant cavity in a strong field searches for microwave axion conversion; the same data also constrain dark photons and scalar dark matter.

status.label: Multiphase project: completed experiments alongside further construction / design
status.evidence: An official center report states that the Swinburne low-frequency branch began data-taking; the main experiment and branch are grouped in one series record.

timeline.event: Limits on Dark Photons, Scalars, and Axion-Electromagnetodynamics with The ORGAN Experiment

collaboration.name: ORGAN Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

phases.name: ORGAN low-frequency branch
phases.description: An official center report states that Swinburne began data-taking in 2026.

results.summary: ORGAN 1a constrains axions and alternative dark-matter models; sensitivities of subsequent phases are projections rather than achieved results.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
